headline: AI “mind-reading” tool reconstructs what you’re looking at from a brain scan
summary: Scientists hope this tool could eventually reconstruct a person's inner thoughts, mental images, or even their dreams, opening new possibilities for understanding the human mind.
details: Researchers have developed an AI tool capable of reconstructing visual information directly from brain scans. This groundbreaking technology can accurately recreate images a person is currently viewing by analyzing their brain activity.

Scientists are optimistic about the future applications of this 'mind-reading' AI. They believe it could eventually be used to visualize a person's inner thoughts, mental images, and even their dreams, offering unprecedented insights into consciousness.

headline: Neurable unveils brain-scanning headphones to fine-tune focus, available October for $499
summary: The Neurable One headphones feature 12 EEG sensors and passively monitor brain activity to improve concentration. They cost $499 and will be available in October.
details: Neurable has officially unveiled its own brain-scanning headphones, the Neurable One, priced at $499 and set to be available in October from their website. These headphones integrate 12 EEG sensors within the earpads to monitor brain waves, aiming to help users concentrate on tasks like working, studying, or gaming.

Unlike previous iterations, the Neurable One passively monitors brain activity as soon as they are worn, similar to a fitness tracker. When distraction is detected, the headphones play a subtle ping to re-engage focus. If burnout is identified, they recommend a break.

The companion app tracks eight brain metrics and offers features for meditation and sleep. For meditation, it can pause guided sessions when you're in a flow state and resume if your mind wanders. For naps, it can gradually lower volume as it detects you falling asleep.

Neurable points to previous research with the Mayo Clinic, which showed a 30 percent increase in focus for users of Neurable's headset compared to other focus techniques. The study also noted a 10 percent drop in end-of-day burnout and an increase in happiness.

The product is not classified as a medical device and is not designed to diagnose or treat conditions. Neurable has committed to not selling any collected brain data and not using it for advertising purposes, ensuring user privacy.
